name: St. Benedict's Abbey bells Atchison KS close 9-28-2019.wav
description: Bells ring at St. Benedict's Abbey in Atchison Kansas for the noon hour. I'm sitting on the steps facing Division Street between 2nd and 3rd. The bells begin to ring and I get up and slowly walk east to get a bit closer to the sound. You hear my cane tap a couple times in the background. Some traffic is heard on Division which is busy on a Saturday. You can hear a few crickets in the background. A crow caws in the distance near the beginning, a distant call from another bird is heard a bit later. Recorded in Goldwave with an Asus laptop in my backpack with Microsoft Lifecam 3000 poking out of a small compartment and clothespinned to the bag to cut down on noise when I walk. It has a borrowed sock on it to block out the wind. The only production is a (reduce peaks) with Goldwave's native compressor and raised the overall volume. This is part of a 40 minute walk I made from home to the Abbey and back to get a good recording of the bells. I'll post more of the walk later.

name: 260825_184633-2_FR_Greatest_chimes_at_Notre_Dame_de_Paris_Cathedral
description:
Greatest chimes at Notre Dame de Paris (Grand Solemnel). 
I made this recording right in front of Notre Dame de Paris Cathedral (Paris, France) during a warm and pleasant summer evening. 
At the beginning of the file, one can hear tourists and believers, a distant brass-band playing in the street on the right, as well as traffic in the distance, and tourist-boats passing by on the river Seine. 
Then, a few seconds later, the biggest bell (called Bourdon Emmanuel) starts to ring, followed by all the other bells of the cathedral to perform the 'Grand Solemnel' or 'Grand Plenum' (greatest chimes only played for the greatest Catholic and National occasions like Christmas, the election of a new Pope, the commemoration of the 1918 Armistice or the Liberation of Paris on August 25 1944). 
Recorded in August 2026 with a Zoom H5studio and Rycote CA-08 stereo pair in quasi ORTF configuration. 
Fade in/out applied in Audacity. 
(If you want to use this sound as a mono audio file, you may have to delete one channel to avoid phase issues).

name: Altenthann – Isolated Bavarian Church Bell at Distance (300 m, Open Window, Post‑Rain Ambience) - 260224_002
description:
Altenthann – Isolated Bavarian Church Bell at Distance (300 m, Open Window, Post‑Rain Ambience)

UCS Category: AMBIENCE
UCS Subcategory: RELIGIOUS
CatID / CatShort: AMBRlgn / AMB

This field recording captures a Bavarian Catholic church bell ringing in the quiet rural village of Altenthann (Regensburg District, Bavaria, Germany). The bell tower is positioned approximately 300 meters from the microphone location. The Zoom F3 recorder was placed at an open window of a residential building, oriented sideways to the church, creating a naturally diffused yet clearly isolated bell timbre.
The bell tone appears clean, resonant, and spatially distant, with a pronounced fundamental frequency and well‑defined overtones characteristic of traditional Bavarian cast‑bronze church bells. The recording preserves the long, open‑air decay and natural reflections across the surrounding village structures and winter landscape.
The session took place on a December day after a light rain shower, just as the sun began to break through, resulting in a calm, crisp acoustic environment. Subtle rural ambience remains audible in the background — faint village noise, soft environmental stillness, and distant, minimal traffic typical for the region — all low enough not to mask the bell signal.
Captured at 48 kHz / 32‑bit floating point, using Immersive Soundscape "The Earthside" Omni microphones with a Jecklin Disc, the recording provides:

wide yet natural stereo imaging
realistic localization of the bell tower
full harmonic body of the bell
atmospheric sense of distance and space

Processing was intentionally minimal:
gentle high‑pass filtering and slight gain adjustment. No EQ, no noise reduction, no transient shaping. The result is a raw, authentic representation of a Bavarian village bell in natural winter ambience.
Use cases: film/documentary atmospheres, cathedral/ritual sound design, historic ambience beds, rural establishing shots, spatial audio design, bell‑tone analysis, heritage archiving.

⚙️ Technical Specs

Recorder: Zoom F3
Microphones: Immersive Soundscape The Earthside (Omni)
Technique: Jecklin Disc, open‑window placement
Sampling: 48 kHz • 32‑bit float
Processing: gentle HPF, minimal gain adjustment, otherwise RAW
Distance to source: approx. 300 meters
Location: Altenthann (93177), Regensburg District, Bavaria, Germany
Weather: Winter day, post‑rain, sunlight breaking through
Setting: Quiet rural residential area

name: Short Church Bell Ring with Rural Ambience & Birds (High‑Resolution Snippet) Altenthann – 260303_001
description:
Altenthann – Short Church Bell Ring with Rural Ambience & Birds (High‑Resolution Snippet)
UCS: AMBIENCE → RELIGIOUS (AMBRlgn / AMB)
This short high‑resolution excerpt captures the distinct Catholic church bell of the Bavarian village Altenthann (Regensburg District, Germany). Extracted from a longer ambience recording, the snippet focuses on a single clear bell‑ringing event, preserving the natural resonance, harmonic spread, and spatial decay characteristic of traditional cast‑bronze village bells.
Although isolated, the bell is embedded within the authentic rural ambience of the village:

gentle post‑rain quietness
distant birdsong from multiple species
soft, unobtrusive village background noise
clean sense of space and outdoor air

This long‑duration field recording captures the peaceful early‑morning soundscape of Altenthann, a quiet rural community in the district of Regensburg, Germany. Recorded around 06:00 on May 30th, 2025, the session documents the gentle awakening of the village and its surrounding nature.
Using a matched stereo pair of Lewitt LCT 040 small‑diaphragm condenser microphones arranged in an ORTF configuration and connected to a Zoom F6 (recorded at 48 kHz / 32‑bit float and later converted to 24‑bit FLAC), the setup provides a natural stereo image with precise localization and a realistic sense of acoustic depth. The ORTF technique captures the environment with a balanced blend of clarity, width, and spatial accuracy—ideal for portraying the subtle dynamics of an early rural morning.
The ambience is shaped primarily by natural sounds: birdsong from various species, soft cooing of doves, and the distinct crowing of a rooster as the day begins. These elements create a lively yet calm morning atmosphere characteristic of a Bavarian countryside village. In the distance, faint light traffic emerges softly beneath the natural layer, adding a subtle sense of human presence without disturbing the tranquility of the scene.
One notable element is the gentle ringing of church bells in the background—a defining feature of small Bavarian communities—providing a slow, rhythmic anchor within the evolving soundscape.
Overall, this recording offers a serene and detailed portrayal of village life waking up at dawn. It is well suited for ambience libraries, documentaries, nature sound compositions, rural soundscapes, or any project seeking an authentic early‑morning atmosphere from the Bavarian countryside.

The area north of this meander, which is now south of the river Maas, remained part of Gelderland as the Gelderse Waarden until 1958. name: floodplain river Maas  village Hedikhuizen Netherlands 7 pm 250420_1075
description:
Windy floodplains of the Meuse River in the Netherlands on an early evening in April. Local traffic drives across the dyke on the other side. A far church bell telling it is seven. In the distant stables, cows moo incessantly sometimes. Far dog’s. Cows that are content do not moo. All kinds of birds know that it is spring and announce it loudly. A fast boat and inland vessel. High in the sky, some planes and choppers. And rest, a lot of rest in the wind.
About the picture A peaceful and expansive landscape unfolds on the riverbank of the Meuse near Hedikhuizen. At the bottom of the dike, a microphone stands on a tripod, ready to capture the sounds of nature. The dike and floodplains are covered with fresh green grass and bordered by tall reeds and yellow flowers. On the right-hand side is a wooden information board with a map for cyclists who come here to enjoy the view. And on both sides of the river further on are a few trees, their silhouettes outlined against a grey, cloudy sky. The openness of the landscape is typical of the banks of the Meuse in this part of the river, which flows from France in this direction.

About the floodplain The floodplain near Hedikhuizen is an ecologically valuable area along the Meuse River, with a rich history and an important role in water management and nature development. The floodplains are the low-lying lands between the river and the winter dyke. At Hedikhuizen, they form a characteristic part of the Meuse landscape, with a mix of nature, cultural history and hydrological functions. The floodplain consists of grasslands, reed beds and marshy areas. This variety provides habitat for numerous species, including water birds, amphibians and insects. Here you will find species such as the yellow wagtail, reed warbler, and sometimes even the beaver. The flora includes marsh plants such as cattail, meadowsweet, and marsh marigold. Due to its relative tranquillity and limited development, the area is attractive to breeding birds and wintering waterfowl. The dyke and floodplain are accessible via various footpaths. Cyclists can cycle for miles along the dykes, which are closed to motor vehicles.
